content_blocks.title: Stage 01 — User Research, Discovery & Information Architecture

content.description: The empirical foundation of product design. Anchors solutions in genuine user psychology through rigorous qualitative inquiry, behavioral telemetry, journey mapping, and structural information hierarchy.

papers.name: User Discovery & Usability Telemetry
papers.meta: Generative Research · Evaluative Testing · Cohort Analysis
papers.desc: Synthesizing raw user problems into structured insights through interviews, surveys, telemetry analytics, and usability benchmarks.
topics: Semi-structured user interviews and contextual inquiry methods
Usability testing protocols: moderated vs unmoderated task analysis
Quantitative metrics: System Usability Scale (SUS), Single Ease Question (SEQ), and Task Success Rate
Customer Journey Mapping (CJM), empathy matrices, and behavioral persona synthesis
Competitive landscape auditing and heuristic feature gap matrices

papers.name: Mental Models, Ontologies & Navigation
papers.meta: Card Sorting · Tree Testing · Structural Site Hierarchies
papers.desc: Structuring product content and navigation paths to reflect intuitive mental models, minimizing cognitive load and cognitive friction.
topics: Open and closed card sorting methodologies for taxonomic classification
Tree testing for navigational hierarchy validation and category labeling
Object-Oriented UX (OOUX): defining core objects, relationships, and actions
Sitemap architecture and multi-tier navigation paradigms (nested, drill-down, hub-and-spoke)
Search indexing, facet taxonomy, and breadcrumb navigation schemes

callout.title: Research Anchoring Rule
callout.text: Design without research is decoration. Every layout, affordance, and flow must be defensible through concrete user quotes, analytics drop-off points, or validated usability benchmarks. Assumptions must be formulated as testable hypotheses before high-fidelity visual design begins.

content.description: Translating research insights into high-functioning interaction systems. Covers rapid low-fidelity wireframing, behavioral micro-interactions, responsive layout logic, and realistic state prototyping in Figma and Protopie.

papers.name: Low-to-Mid Fidelity Flow Architecture
papers.meta: User Flows · Heuristics · Edge Case Coverage
papers.desc: Drafting structural wireframes that map out complete operational paths, user forks, error boundaries, and edge states.
topics: User flow diagramming and state transition mapping (happy path vs failure modes)
Wireframing with strict layout grids (8pt spatial system) and visual hierarchy
Applying Nielsen Norman Group’s 10 Usability Heuristics to workflow design
Comprehensive edge case specification: empty states, timeout states, zero-data states, and permissions gates
Fitts’s Law, Hick’s Law, and Miller’s Law applied to button placement and form completion

papers.name: Interactive Prototyping & Motion Choreography
papers.desc: Building realistic interactive prototypes with natural physics-based motion to test complex user scenarios with real stakeholders.
topics: Figma prototyping: Smart Animate, interactive components, variables, and boolean conditions
Advanced micro-interactions with Protopie (sensor inputs, conditional logic, formula calculations)
Functional animation principles: spatial continuity, focus management, and transition easing (cubic-bezier)
Micro-haptic and auditory feedback design for critical user confirmation triggers
Rapid stakeholder walkthroughs and clickable testing protocol

callout.title: Edge Case Specification Protocol
callout.text: A designer is evaluated by their edge cases, not their happy path. Production-ready designs must specify: (1) Empty states with clear calls-to-action, (2) Network latency skeletons, (3) Boundary inputs (1-character vs 10,000-character truncation), and (4) Reversible destructive actions (undo toasts over modal confirmation).

content.description: Constructing unified, reusable component ecosystems across web and native mobile platforms. Focuses on W3C Design Tokens, Figma variant architecture, WCAG 2.2 accessibility compliance, and developer parity.

papers.name: Design Tokens & Atomic Components
papers.meta: W3C Token Specs · Multi-Brand Theming · Auto Layout 5.0
papers.desc: Architecting atomic design libraries in Figma that mirror code components (React/Tailwind) via semantic tokens and variables.
topics: 3-Tier Design Token Architecture: Global (Raw), Semantic (Alias), and Component tokens
Multi-brand and dark mode theming using Figma Variables and Modes
Atomic component modeling: Atoms (Buttons, Inputs), Molecules (Search bars), Organisms (Headers)
Advanced Auto Layout: flex wrapping, absolute positioning within auto layout, and responsive min/max constraints
Component governance: versioning, deprecation lifecycle, and documentation in Storybook/Zeroheight

papers.name: WCAG 2.2 Compliance & Developer Spec Handoff
papers.meta: WCAG 2.2 AA/AAA · Screen Readers · Dev Mode Specs
papers.desc: Ensuring digital products are inclusive for all users regardless of ability, while generating pixel-perfect technical handoff specs for engineering.
topics: WCAG 2.2 Guidelines: AA and AAA compliance across contrast ratios (4.5:1 text, 3:1 graphical elements)
Semantic HTML mapping: headings (H1–H6), landmarks (main, nav), button vs anchor tags, and ARIA roles
Keyboard navigation flows: logical tab index order, visible focus rings, and skip links
Figma Dev Mode specs: redlining, CSS snippet generation, spacing tokens, and asset optimization (SVG/WebP)
Color-blindness simulation (Deuteranopia, Protanopia) and motion sensitivity fallbacks (prefers-reduced-motion)

callout.title: Token Governance & Dev Parity
callout.text: A design system is only as strong as its code parity. Semantic tokens (e.g., color.background.surface.default) must match 1:1 between Figma variables and the frontend CSS/Tailwind config. Changes must be governed with semantic versioning to prevent breaking component changes in production.

content_blocks.title: Stage 04 — Product Strategy, Metrics & Design Leadership

content.description: Elevating product design from visual craft to executive business impact. Connecting design decisions directly to acquisition, conversion, retention, North Star metrics, and cross-functional leadership.

papers.name: Product Telemetry & A/B Experimentation
papers.meta: North Star Metrics · Retention Cohorts · Growth Funnels
papers.desc: Using product analytics tools (Mixpanel, Amplitude, PostHog) to identify drop-off friction and orchestrate continuous A/B experimentation.
topics: Defining product North Star metrics and input metric drivers
Funnel analysis: diagnosing drop-offs in onboarding, checkout, and activation flows
Designing rigorous A/B experiment variants with hypothesis-driven design changes
Measuring qualitative feedback alongside quantitative telemetry (NPS vs CSAT vs CES)
Design ROI formulation: translating usability improvements into quantifiable revenue & retention uplift

papers.name: Case Study Architecture & Design Critique
papers.meta: Portfolio Presentation · Whiteboard Challenges · Stakeholder Alignment
papers.desc: Structuring high-impact case studies that tell a compelling narrative of problem discovery, iteration, technical trade-offs, and measurable outcomes.
topics: Structuring portfolio case studies: Context, Problem, Constraints, Hypothesis, Iterations, and Outcome
Conducting structured design critiques: providing actionable feedback and defending trade-offs without ego
Executive stakeholder management: pitching design proposals to C-suite and engineering leads
Live whiteboard design challenge mastery: framing ambiguous product briefs in 45-minute live interviews
App critique framework: evaluating mobile/web apps on interaction elegance, business model, and information hierarchy

callout.title: Business Impact Multiplier
callout.text: Elite product designers speak the language of business. During portfolio evaluations and executive reviews, candidates who clearly demonstrate how their UX decisions increased activation rates by 18% or decreased churn by 12% outperform designers who only present polished visual mockups.

content.sub: Phased 12 to 18-Month Mastery Protocol · Visual Foundations to Enterprise Product Systems

prerequisites: Portfolio Requirement: Minimum 3 comprehensive, documented case studies showcasing end-to-end design thinking from discovery and wireframes to component tokens and shipped impact.
Tooling Mastery: Expert-level fluency in Figma (Auto Layout 5.0, Component Variants, Variables, Dev Mode) and modern prototyping suites (Protopie / Framer).
Design System Literacy: Deep understanding of atomic design principles, W3C design tokens, multi-platform design guidelines (Apple HIG, Google Material Design 3).
Cross-Functional Fluency: Proven capacity to partner with frontend engineering teams, read basic HTML/CSS structures, and participate in sprint planning rituals.

roadmap.title: Low-to-High Fidelity Prototyping & Edge Cases

roadmap.title: Design Tokens, Atomic Systems & WCAG Accessibility

roadmap.title: Product Telemetry, Growth Funnels & A/B Experimentation
